extracted.intended_audience: organizations, academic centers, researchers, and policy groups seeking Hewlett Foundation Cyber Initiative funding or aligning work with the initiative's priorities
extracted.subtask_description: A program-level overview of the Hewlett Foundation's Cyber Initiative (2014–2023) describing the initiative's goals, strategic focus, and the kinds of work and institutions it aimed to support. Useful for applicants and partners aligning proposals with the foundation's priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive definition, research, and management
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation makes grants to proactively define, research, and manage the burgeoning intersections between people and digital technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis is on proactive, research-oriented work that shapes understanding and governance of digital-technology impacts rather than reactive operational responses to immediate incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field building through multidisciplinary solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cyber Initiative seeks to cultivate a field that develops thoughtful, multidisciplinary solutions to complex cyber challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority to proposals that bring together technical and non-technical disciplines to address complexity; supports efforts that establish norms, frameworks, or interdisciplinary communities rather than siloed single-discipline work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalyze better policy outcomes for societies
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should catalyze better policy outcomes for the benefit of societies around the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for projects with clear paths to influencing policy debates, decision-makers, or public understanding at national or international levels; global societal benefit is an expressed objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build core institutions with deep expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a set of core institutions with sufficient depth of expertise to deliver solutions that take competing values and trade-offs to pressing cyber policy challenges seriously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund institution-building (e.g., centers) that can sustain deep, rigorous analysis; emphasis on institutions able to handle trade-offs among values (security, privacy, openness, etc.). Examples: support for multidisciplinary cyber policy centers at MIT, UC Berkeley, and Stanford.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a talent pipeline with mixed skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a talent pipeline to produce experts with the necessary mix of technical and non-technical skills and knowledge to staff these and other institutions, including government and industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports education, training, and workforce-development activities that produce practitioners fluent in both technical concepts and policy/ethics/communications — i.e., interdisciplinary capacity-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support infrastructure for translation and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the development of infrastructure to translate and disseminate the work of these institutions that can be understood and used by decision makers and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for tools, platforms, communications, or intermediary organizations that make research actionable and accessible to policymakers, journalists, and the public; measurable reach or usability for decision-makers is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality and independence from policy outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation is explicitly agnostic as to specific policy outcomes; unlike government or industry, it is a neutral player not motivated by profit, politics, or self-interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded work should reflect independence and rigorous analysis rather than advocacy for predetermined outcomes; the aim is to generate robust debate and analysis to inform better policy, not to push a partisan agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-limited, strategic focus rather than immediate incident response
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cyber Initiative is meant to be time-limited (initial five-year commitment, renewed through 2023) and the Foundation is not responsible for responding to the myriad latest threats and challenges that government and industry must triage each day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for strategic, long-term work (norms, institutions, education, translation) over operational incident response or short-term remediation; projects should align with the initiative's finite timeframe and strategic objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on thinking through strategic implications of connectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Need to put more thought into how a connected world changes the balance of power among states and how to manage that, analogous to past responses to chemical weapons, nuclear weapons, and drones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages research and policy work that considers geopolitical and strategic dimensions of cyber and connected technologies — high-level, comparative, and historically informed analyses are appropriate.
